answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, causing influence to decay when paths repeatedly cross weakly connected regions. An adversarial Sybil cluster S has a sparse boundary and low conductance, φ(S)=cut(S,¬S)/vol(S), which limits its escape probability. Min-cut transitivity bounds therefore cap its stationary mass and aggregate voting weight, even when it disguises its topology as a canyon, bridge, or wharf.
